cultural.vision_reason: This is a classic Ewe strip-woven hammock (kete-style narrow-strip weaving with supplementary weft motifs, animals, objects, inscriptions, and tasseled fringe), a well-documented Ewe/Ghanaian textile tradition.

physical.title: hammock
physical.summary: Hammock composed of hand-woven narrow strips of imported European cotton hand-sewn together along the selvedges; there are eight strips with extensive decoration, and two along the edges that have minimal decoration. The hammock is two-sided, with the cloth folded to give two different panels on either side with different designs. The monochrome ground weave on both sides is plain woven with orange/brown in both warp and weft. There is extensive decoration formed by blocks of coloured weft using a second pair of heddles that block out the ground weave; between these are areas of with patterns woven in discontinuous supplementary weft using yarn coloured in light and dark green, orange, yellow, red, black, purple and blue. These patterns consist of geometric patterns and representations of animals. Along the centre of the hammock on the upper side is woven the text "Walter Bell Rest A While" in supplementary weft. Along the edges of the warp are tassels made from yellow, orange, purple, red, green, blue, grey and white cotton. At the ends of the hammock, the warps have been plaited together and wrapped in coloured cotton in order to attach carrying poles to the hammock.
